title: Protocol for the determination of intracellular phase separation thresholds
protocol: Seed cells to achieve 40% confluency on the day of transfection.
Determine optimal confluency for transfection based on cell type.
For G3BP knockout U2OS cells, seed 20,000 cells per well in a 4-well chamber slide 16–24 hours before transfection.
Dilute 200 ng of plasmid DNA containing GFP-G3BP1 or the gene of interest in Buffer EC from the Effectene Transfection Reagent kit for a total volume of 60 μL.
Add 1.6 μL of Enhancer to the diluted DNA, vortex for 1 s, and briefly spin down the mixture.
Incubate the mixture at 20°C–25°C for 2–5 minutes.
Add 5 μL of Effectene Transfection Reagent to the mixture, vortex for 10 seconds, and briefly spin down the mixture.
Incubate the final mixture at 20°C–25°C for 5–10 minutes.
Remove cells from incubator and gently aspirate growth medium.
Add 350 μL of fresh growth medium to each well.
Add 350 μL of growth medium to the transfection complex.
Mix well by pipetting.
Add the transfection complex dropwise onto cells.
Gently swirl the slide to distribute the transfection complex.
Return cells to the incubator.
Remove cells from the incubator after 24 h.
Gently aspirate growth media.
Add 400 μL of fresh growth medium.
Return cells to the incubator for an additional 24 h.
Transiently transfect G3BP knockout U2OS cells with GFP-G3BP1 for live-cell imaging.
Treat transfected cells with 500 μM sodium arsenite and collect images over 2 hours.
Quantify the GFP intensity of each cell before sodium arsenite treatment using ImageJ.
Perform live-cell imaging on transfected cells and subsequently fix and immunostain for G3BP1.
Conduct live-cell and immunofluorescent imaging on wild-type cells lacking GFP but stained with G3BP antibody.
Take a multipoint time-lapse, imaging each field every 40 seconds for two iterations.
Set up a time-lapse “T-Series” in Prairie View to run at all XYZ stage locations.
Dilute the 50 mM stock solution of sodium arsenite with growth medium to prepare a final concentration of 1 mM.
Add 400 μL of the 1 mM sodium arsenite solution to cells (cultured in 400 μL of growth medium) for sufficient mixing without disturbing the slide.
Immediately begin a multipoint time-lapse and collect images for 2 hours.
Create an XY table in GraphPad Prism with one row for each cell.
Enter GFP intensity as the X value and stress granule initiation time as the Y value.
Select a region of interest from the background and measure its mean intensity using Analyze > Measure for background correction.
Quantify the GFP intensity of each cell from the frame before sodium arsenite addition.
Use the “Freehand Selections” tool in ImageJ to outline a cell.
Determine the total cell integrated density, area, and mean intensities using the Analyze > Measure command.
Outline the nucleus using the “Freehand Selections” tool and measure its integrated density and area.
Subtract the nuclear integrated density from the total cell integrated density.
Subtract the nuclear area from the total cell area.
Calculate the corrected mean cytoplasmic intensity: (Total cell integrated density − Nuclear integrated density)/(Total cell area − Nuclear area) − Mean background intensity.
Identify the time after sodium arsenite treatment when two stress granules form to measure the stress granule initiation time of each cell.
Transfect G3BP knockout cells with GFP-G3BP1.
Determine GFP intensity at single-cell resolution by live-cell imaging 48 hours post transfection.
Immunostain the cells for G3BP1 and correlate fluorescence from immunostaining to previously measured GFP intensity on a cell-by-cell basis.
Seed either wild-type or mutant cells.
Transfect G3BP knockout cells with GFP-G3BP1.
Wait 24 hours after transfection.
Aspirate the growth media.
Gently wash cells.
Seed 500 μL of wild-type (or mutant) cells in the same well as the transfected cells.
Determine the optimal number of cells to seed after transfection.
For wild-type U2OS cells, seed 10,000 cells per well in a 4-well chamber slide 24 h after transfection.
Return cells to the incubator for an additional 24 h.
Perform live-cell imaging as described in steps 12–14.
Capture images of the selected cells.
Save the stage locations of the selected fields to assist in cell relocation after immunostaining.
Prepare fresh Fixing Solution for immunostaining.
Gently wash cells with 1 mL of PBS.
Fix cells with 500 μL of Fixing Solution for 15 min at 20°C–25°C.
Wash cells 2× with 500 μL of PBS for 5 min.
Permeabilize cells with 500 μL of Blocking Solution for 20 min at 4°C.
Dilute primary antibody in Blocking Solution and spin down at 21,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Add 250 μL of diluted primary antibody to cells and incubate 12–18 h at 4°C or 1 h at 20°C–25°C.
Incubate slide in a container with a wet paper towel as a humidifier for 12–18 hours.
Increase volume of diluted primary antibody to prevent cells from drying out if necessary.
Wash cells three times with 500 μL of Wash Solution for 5 minutes each.
Dilute secondary antibody 1:500 in Blocking Solution and spin down at 21,000 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Add 500 μL of diluted secondary antibody to cells and cover with foil.
Incubate cells for 30 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Wash cells three times with 500 μL of Wash Solution for 5 minutes each.
Add 500 μL of PBS to cells.
Return slide to the microscope in the same orientation as previously imaged.
Set the 488 and 561 nm lasers to 80 power and 100 ms exposure time using a 35 μm slit.
Identify and image cells that lack GFP but exhibit signal from antibody staining.
Create an XY table in GraphPad Prism with one row for each transfected cell.
Enter GFP intensity from live-cell imaging as the X value.
Enter immunofluorescent intensity from antibody staining as the Y value.
Select a region of interest from the background.
Use the Analyze > Measure command to measure mean intensity for background correction.
Quantify the GFP intensity of each cell from live-cell imaging.
Outline a cell using the “Freehand Selections” tool in ImageJ.
Determine total cell integrated density, area, and mean intensities.
Outline the nucleus using the “Freehand Selections” tool.
Determine the integrated density and area of the nucleus.
Subtract the nuclear integrated density from the total cell measurements to determine cytoplasmic intensity.
Calculate corrected mean cytoplasmic intensity: (Total cell integrated density − Nuclear integrated density)/(Total cell area − Nuclear area) − Mean background intensity.
Quantify the immunofluorescent intensity of each cell from antibody staining in the same way.
Plot each cell as a single point with GFP intensity on the X-axis and immunofluorescent intensity on the Y-axis.
Perform a simple linear regression analysis within GraphPad Prism to model the relationship between GFP intensity and immunofluorescent intensity.
Quantify the immunofluorescent intensity of each wild-type (or mutant) cell from antibody staining.
Determine the GFP equivalent of the average measured immunofluorescent intensity from wild-type (or mutant) cells using the calculated linear regression line.
